clue.text: Bosom oddly is not firm, partner!

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep the odd-numbered letters running through the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone protests to their partner that their chest is not as firm as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on across 'is not firm, partner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosom friend is a very close one, and close in that personal sense is the adjective here.

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A cult group takes in the cult's own leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a religious faction, often a cult in the loose sense.

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: A plea to support a foolish person on the spot, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' keeps alternate letters of 'in situ', the 1st, 3rd and 5th.
explanation.definitionFit: To support someone is to help them, a straight synonym.

parts.note: a bloke is a man
a date is a romantic outing

explanation.surface: A man is ordered out on a romantic date.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official order or instruction, so a command.

definitions.meaning: inhaling, as in the medical sense of drawing breath or matter in

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both drawing in breath and a strong hope or ambition, two separate senses.

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Part of a church loses a hard-line ban.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel something is to call it off or ban it.

indicators.note: partially filling says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A submarine, half full of water, sinks easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'founders' and the start of 'easily'; 'founders' looks like a verb about sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means below the sea's surface, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lose track of dispatch on motorway

indicators.note: on means the killing word is placed after the road abbreviation

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
to dispatch is to kill, so slay

explanation.surface: Losing track of someone dispatched on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway, written with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it where you cannot find it, losing track of it.

clue.text: Horse fly, then result is rearing

indicators.note: rearing in a down clue means the letters rise, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
a sum is the result of adding

explanation.surface: A horse rears when a fly lands on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing' turns the whole run of the two pieces upward, giving the letters in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild horse of the American plains.

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: An uprising breaks out in open disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a rising in open tumult is a disturbance in the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public uprising, which is what the clue describes.

indicators.note: grips means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: instinct is intuition
DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: A detective's vague hunch gets a grip on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Indistinct means blurred or unclear, so vague.

parts.note: Yank looks like a verb meaning pull hard, but means American: the US word for a tap

explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a water tap by this name, so it is a tap in US English.

indicators.note: cracking means the second piece breaks into the first

parts.note: clever means cunning
someone who opposes is anti

explanation.surface: Someone contrary breaks into the crafty setter Beam.
explanation.walkthrough: Beam is the setter of this puzzle, so the question mark flags the definition as a playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a beam fixed at one end only, projecting out, as in some bridges.

clue.text: Hardship of endless hail in track

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a trail is a track

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: Hardship from a hailstorm on the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the Latin greeting before it goes inside; 'hail' looks like weather in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful toil or labour, a synonym for hardship.

parts.note: pride suggests self-respect, but a pride is a group of lions, so a lioness

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lion-like, and a lioness lives in a pride.

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: noise is sound
a gong is slang for a medal, here OM, the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A gong being struck makes an offensive noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul or offensive, especially in smell.

clue.text: Playing when before time around net

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the next
around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: as means when
to net is to gain

explanation.surface: A game of tennis, playing up to the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' as in a team playing Arsenal, meaning facing them.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport, playing a team means competing with them, that is opposing them.

clue.text: Raising head of whip in flogging

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to flog is slang for to sell

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter

explanation.surface: A raised welt left by a whip in a flogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' is British slang for selling, not beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A raising is a raised lump or bump, which is the noun sense here.

clue.text: Undressed, dropping one quietly, and streaked

indicators.note: dropping says a letter falls out of the word

parts.note: stripped means undressed
P is piano, the musical term for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone stripped off, dropped one item quietly, and streaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' says only one of the two P letters goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Striped means marked with streaks or bands.

clue.text: One favours best English literature first

parts.note: 1st, read as IST

explanation.surface: A snob prefers the best English literature above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, and the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes the best should be favoured over others is a snob of this kind.

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter
late means recently, as in of late
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is thrilled at being given diamonds lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means overjoyed, a near synonym of ecstatic.

indicators.note: swallowing means the first piece takes the other inside

parts.note: finer means better
G is short for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone better at drinking downs a grand dram.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger of spirit is a measure about as deep as a finger, a dram.

indicators.note: exteriors says to keep only the outside letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A painting by Canaletto shows fancy building fronts.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'exteriors' is not an instruction but fodder: its own outer letters give ES.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting done on wet plaster.

parts.note: a cat is a feline
ego stands for self-regard
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: A selfish cat demands a pay rise to show its class.
explanation.definitionFit: To categorise is to sort into classes, the verb sense of class.

indicators.note: deducting means letters are taken out

parts.note: really means actually
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bank actually takes a pound off you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is a verb, as in bank on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on them, so the verb means count on.

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters go upward, read backwards
embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: The Queen is warmly cheered, raising her esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' builds the inner piece first, then 'raised' turns the whole result upward, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to esteem them highly, as a verb.

clue.text: Go back westward in Pembrokeshire, generally

indicators.note: westward says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Turning back westward through Pembrokeshire, as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue westward means right to left; Pembrokeshire is a Welsh county.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise is to break one's word, exactly this verb.

clue.text: Going outside, catching cold, causing fever

indicators.note: catching means the first piece holds the other inside

parts.note: exiting is going out
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Going out in the cold gives you a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrilling stirs one up, causing a fever of excitement.
